record.paper_title: Constructive Field Theory and Applications: Perspectives and Open Problems
record.original_question: Find a direct proof of convergence of the Mayer expansion for dipoles at low activity, without relying on a cluster expansion, for a dipole-dipole interaction smoothed at short distance so that it is stable.

evidence.quote: Find a direct proof of convergence of the Mayer expansion for dipoles at low activity (which does not use a cluster expansion). The dipole-dipole interaction should be smoothed at short distance so that it is stable.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a classical gas of dipoles in $\mathbb{R}^d$ (with $d\ge 2$) in the grand canonical ensemble at activity $z>0$ and inverse temperature $\beta>0$. A configuration of $N$ dipoles is given by positions $x_1,\dots,x_N\in\mathbb{R}^d$ and orientations (unit vectors) $\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_N\in S^{d-1}$. Two dipoles at positions $x,y$ with orientations $\sigma,\tau$ interact through a pair potential

$$V(x,\sigma;y,\tau) \;=\; (\sigma\cdot\nabla_x)(\tau\cdot\nabla_y)\,G(x-y),$$

where $G$ is the Coulomb (or otherwise long-range) Green's function, regularized at short distance by a smooth ultraviolet cutoff $\chi$ so that the resulting two-body potential $V$ is stable, i.e., there exists $B\ge 0$ such that

$$\sum_{1\le i<j\le N} V(x_i,\sigma_i;x_j,\sigma_j) \;\ge\; -B\,N$$

for all $N\ge 1$ and all configurations.

The (finite-volume) pressure admits the formal Mayer series
$$\beta p(z) \;=\; \sum_{n\ge 1} b_n\, z^n,$$
where $b_n$ are the Mayer coefficients obtained by summing connected graphs on $n$ vertices with Mayer factors $f_{ij}=e^{-\beta V_{ij}}-1$ and integrating over positions and orientations.

Problem. Prove directly, without invoking any cluster expansion (e.g., without using a polymer or tree-graph expansion that organizes the activity into renormalized polymers), that the Mayer series for the dipole gas converges absolutely on a disc of positive radius around $z=0$. Equivalently, exhibit constants $C,R>0$ (depending only on $\beta$, $d$, and the ultraviolet cutoff) such that $|b_n|\le C^n$ and the series converges for $|z|<R$, with the proof proceeding by direct estimation of the Mayer coefficients.
artifact.status_search_result: Partial progress exists: direct bounds on Mayer coefficients of the 2D dipole gas at high temperature/low activity have been established without multiscale/renormalization-group analysis, exploiting a so-called θ-symmetry of the dipole-dipole interaction, showing Mayer coefficients are finite in the thermodynamic limit. However, a full direct proof of convergence (analyticity in z) of the Mayer expansion without any cluster expansion appears not to be completely settled, and it has been conjectured that θ-symmetry alone is insufficient. Convergence via cluster/renormalization-group expansions is classically known (Brydges–Federbush, Brydges–Kennedy, etc.).

status_evidence.title: Coulomb interaction symmetries and the Mayer series in the two-dimensional dipole gas
status_evidence.snippet: Bounds showing that Mayer coefficients of the 2D dipole gas are finite in the thermodynamic limit without multiscale analysis, using θ-symmetry.
status_evidence.claim: Partial direct results on Mayer coefficients for the dipole gas have been obtained without multiscale analysis.

status_evidence.title: A cluster expansion for dipole gases
status_evidence.snippet: Convergence of the Mayer series for the dipole gas proved via cluster expansion at small activity.
status_evidence.claim: Convergence is known via cluster expansion, but the requested direct (non-cluster) proof remains the open target.

status_evidence.title: On the analyticity of the pressure in the hierarchical dipole gas
status_evidence.snippet: Analyticity of the pressure established for the hierarchical dipole model.
status_evidence.claim: Analyticity is known in hierarchical/RG settings; the fully direct Mayer-expansion proof is the unsolved question.
